findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that a sanitizer bucket in the meat department was not registering levels of quaternary ammonium (0ppm). PIC investigated and found that the source of the sanitizing solution, a hose dispenser from the meat department triple sink, was using hot water, which deactivates the sanitizer in the solution. PIC determined that there was a plumbing issue that was causing hot water to come out of the dispenser without an option to make it cold. A plumber was contacted and arrived during the inspection. In the meantime, the meat department will source its sanitizing solution for surfaces and warewashing from the working sanitizer dispenser from the triple sink in the neighboring deli department. The new sanitizer bucket measured at 200pm for quaternary ammonium. Ensure that all sanitizing solutions are sanitizing at safe and effective concentrations, which is between 200-400ppm for quaternary ammonium, and that sanitizing solutions are created per manufacturer’s instructions.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed that portions of the salad bar are not holding food temperatures at 41F or below. The side closest to the coffee station is holding all foods at 41F or below. The opposite side (closest to the hot wing station) is not holding all temperatures at 41F of below. The areas not holding food at the proper temperature are from the far left side all the way to the lettuce. The following internal temperatures were recorded: chicken 55F, lettuce 50F, green peppers 53F, cheese 54F, and ham 55F. The deli PIC and store manger were instructed to use time-as-control for the temperature control for safety (TCS) foods in the cooler. The foods being temperature controlled are lettuce, mozzarella cheese, blue cheese, feta cheese, chicken, ham, turkey, crab, and eggs. The rest of the non-TCS foods are allowed to remain in the cooler all day. Since all foods had been put into the salad cooler at 9 am they were instructed to discarded all TCS foods at 1 pm. The salad bar only stays open until 4 pm, so all TCS foods will be discarded again when the salad bar closes. The deli PIC will be overseeing that time-as-control is correctly implemented. The store manager stated they will be scheduling maintenance for the salad cooler as soon as possible. Time-as-control must be used for all TCS foods until the salad cooler is properly functioning. The inspector will follow-up on 3/3/2025 to ensure that the salad cooler is cold holding all foods at 41F or below.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following over the course of the inspection today:
- The hand sink in the deli as immediately after the entrance to the deli was not stocked with paper towels or soap. The soap dispenser was empty and open. Per operator, the paer towel dispenser is not functioning. 
- The second hand sink in the deli between the bakery and the deli was stocked with soap but was not stocked with paper towels.
- The hand sink in the meat processing area of the meat department was stocked with soap but not paper towels. Per the meat department operator, he had requested x4 times to have the paper towels stocked and they had not been stocked yet.

In both instances, operators were aware the sinks were improperly stocked. The person-in-charge of the deli left the facility to get chicken tenders from another store. The person-in-charge of the meat department had unfulfilled requests to have the paper towels stocked. 

The combination of violations during the inspection today is incredibly concerning. Staff was completely unable to wash hands WHILE participating in highly risky behavior with a high likelihood of contamination. Hand sinks in this facility have been a recurring problem. Facility fails to treat hand washing as a priority. Facility has been issued a repeat letter and notice to comply already for previous hand washing sink violations. 

Paper towels and soap were restocked during the inspection. Corrected on site. A follow-up is still being issued due to repeated violations and multiple occurrences during the inspection day. Inspector will return on Monday 04/03/2023 to verify compliance with 2017 FDA Food Code requirements.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Inspector observed cooling foods in the walk-in cooler in thin metal pans at temperatures between 65 degrees F and 105 degrees F. The cooling logs were immediately reviewed with person-in-charge and no entries were avaible for today (03/24/2023) despite a black page being presnt in the binder. Person-in-charge stated that the manager who had lef the store briefly had placed the items in the walk-in for cooling and had not updated the log. This was discussed with the manager when she returned to the facility. If cooling logs are facility procedure for ensuring proper cooling, these logs must be maintained. Without proper temperature monitoring and no employee present who can give a time foods went into the critical temperature zone, inspector has no method to verify proper cooling times and temperatures. Ensure that logs are kept as required by store policy and that all cooled foods are cooled to the required temperatures within the correct timeframes. DO NOT rely upon memory for time and temperatures or fill in incorrect temperatures in the logs. A follow-up is issed for 03/27/2023 to ensure compliance.

Upon speaking with PIC, inspector was informed that the ice was from dumping ice water used to cool vegetables. Discussed that hand washing sinks may not be used for any purpose besides hand washing, this includes the dumping of ice/water or other material. Educated PIC on the need to have an accessible hand washing sink at all times and dumping can hamper the ability of employees to wash their hands and cause clogged drains to occur. 

During a prior inspection, hand washing sinks were clogged and draining slowly. This had been repaired. Cease dumping to prevent clogs from occurring in the future as well. This is a repeat violation.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
The flour bin next to the fryers was closed but the handle of the scoop was in the flour on arrival. Ensure that the handles of scoops and other utensils, if stored in the food, are not allowed to touch the food product to prevent cross contamination caused by grabbing the handles. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
A red sanitizer bucket on the deli prep line had a concentration of 0 ppm per test strip reading. Bucket was immediately replaced by employee on line and proper 150 ppm concentration was reached. Corrected on site. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector entered the butchery prep room and observed the slicer and grinder to be soiled with moist, apparently fresh meat. Inspector asked operator how often the slicer and grinder are cleaned. Operator stated that they are cleaned once a day at the end of the day. This is not a proper practice for cleaning food contact surfaces such as grinders and meat slicers. These must be cleaned AT LEAST once every 4 hours. Ensure that cleaning of these surfaces occurs at least every four hours throughout the course of operations. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Facility has cooler procedures in place which are not being followed at this time. A blue binder is kept in the premise which includes all temperature logs used throughout the day. Hot holding temperatures for chicken and other items appear to be up to date. However, temperatures for cooling are not being recorded. Discussed this with PIC who stated that employees are required to complete logs every time they begin cooling but they have not been doing it. Inspector educated on the benefits of keeping logs to allow employees, managers and inspectors to see when items began cooling to ensure compliance with the two-hour to 70 degree and 6 hour to 41 degree requirements. Because logs were not kept and no temperatures were recorded on labels or other locations, PIC and inspector had no way of determining how long items had been cooling for. A tray of meatloaf and a tray of broccoli casserole were discarded voluntarily by person in charge due to being out of temperature. The meatloaf was 100 degrees F and the broccoli casserole was 48 degrees F. Cooling must occur within proper time frames and to proper temperatures. A procedure must be in place and followed to allow for cooling within these parameters. 

3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed the display warmer at the front of the deli department to be holding temperature inconsistently. This is a known issue which PIC states was discussed with maintenance but repairs/replacement have not been completed. If equipment cannot maintain TCS foods at 135 degrees or higher, facility must use time as a pubic health control and have a written procedure in place. No written procedure is in place at this time. However, the log binder states to discard food regardless of temperature after two hours. PIC and inspector have completed time as a control documentation to follow the two-hour time frame indicated in the log binder. Facility will hot hold items in this warmer for no more than two hours and discard and will log those times to ensure compliance. Items which were currently out of temperature and being held were voluntarily reheated to 165 degrees and will be held for an additional two hours before being discarded. Corrected on site. 

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
An unlabeled bottle at the rear of the meat prep room contained an unknown liquid. Ensure that all bottles are labeled with the common name of the liquid. 

7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Display warmer for chicken and other hold holding is not working properly and only intermittently holds temperature of foods at 135 degrees per PIC. Ensure that the warmer is working properly to maintain a temperature of at least 135 F.

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed 8 flies around the hand sink directly to the east of the bakery area and next to the canned storage area. This is a repeat violation from previous inspection. Work with pest control to eliminate flies in the facility. Flies were observed individually and sparsely throughout other areas of the kitchen but in small numbers. Clean facility throughout to eliminate harborage conditions.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Inspector entered the walk-in cooler and noticed that the ambient air flowing from the cooler did not quite feel cold enough. Temperatures on most foods were borderline between approximately 42 degrees F and 45 degrees F. Although PIC is not sure of defrost cycle timing, cooler may have been in defrost because the temperature coming from the blowers began at 44 degrees and dropped rapidly to 39 degrees while inspector was still in the cooler. During this time, water began to spray in large drops from the condenser. PIC states he has never seen that happen before but has noticed a mist from the cooler in the past. Spraying water from mechanical condensers cannot be dripping or spraying onto food stored in the cooler. Food directly in the line of spray was moved to another cooler until the cooler can be fixed. The few uncovered items exposed to the water spray were discarded. Inspector is issuing a follow-up to ensure that mechanical equipment is operating correctly and water spray is no longer spraying before putting food back in the cooler. 

3-305.12: FOOD may not be stored: (A) In locker rooms; (B) In toilet rooms; (C) In dressing rooms; (D) In garbage rooms; (E) In mechanical rooms; (F) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (G) Under leaking water lines, including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads, or under lines on which water has condensed; (H) Under open stairwells; or (I) Under other sources of contamination.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
A wet wiping cloths were observed sitting on the cutting board surface of the meat prep table of the butchery room. Another wet wiping cloth was observed sitting on the grinder in the meat storage area. Wet wiping cloths when not directly in use MAY NOT be stored sitting on surfaces but must be stored in sanitizer buckets. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer solution when not directly in use for wiping surfaces. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The prep and hand washing sinks next to the the fryers, mop sink, and triple sink have caulking that is moldy, deteriorating and/or missing. Re-caulk these areas to ensure that they are smooth, durable, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. This is a repeat violation from prior inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
There is an accumulation of residue and debris and the junction of the wall and floor throughout the facility. Areas underneath large equipment are beginning to accumulate a significant amount of residue and debris. Sides of the fryers between the fryer units are beginning to become heavily soiled with oil and other residue. Between the top and bottom portions of the steam oven is heavily soiled. Clean these areas and ensure that they remain clean to prevent contamination and pests in the facility. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
A personal Bai drink was being stored in the upright freezer in the deli area. Personal drinks must have a designated area for storage. The drink was promptly removed and employees are reminded to store drinks in designated areas. Corrected on site. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Managers in deli and meat departments do not currently have food manager certifications. Store manager was on-site during inspection and has a current food manager certification. Store manager stated 10 people are registered to attend a food manager course to obtain certification on 4/6/22, including the deli and meat department managers. 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Manager entered the meat department and put on gloves to help a customer without first washing their hands. Handwashing upon entering the work area and between tasks as needed were discussed. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, upon entering the work area, before putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Sanitizer bucket was observed in the basin of the handwashing sink in the meat department. Sani-bucket was removed from the handwashing sink. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items in the basin of the handsink for any reason.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towel dispenser was empty at the handwashing sink in the meat department. Paper towels were provided during inspection.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Foods in the deli walk-in cooler were at various stages of the cooling process. Chili Mac began at 9:30am per the label on the container, and the product was still at 70F in the middle. Chili Mac was discarded. Mostaccioli began cooling at 9:45am and had an internal temperature of 65F-67F. Chicken salad prepared with tenders that were cooked and cooled this morning and just mixed about 30 minutes prior to inspection also had an internal temperate of 66F-67F. Temperature of chicken tenders was not checked prior shredding and mixing with ingredients to make chicken salad. Mostaccioli and chicken salad were moved to the freezer to finish rapidly chilling foods. 
Ensure temperatures are monitored during cooling process with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling. 
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 Container of cream cheese and sausage mix in the meat department cooler had a use by date of 3/18. The prep date on the label looked like it said 3/4 or possibly 3/14. Meat department manager discarded the product. 
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-302.12 Meat department only had an infrared thermometer available for monitoring temperatures. Deli manager had an extra digital probe thermometer for use in the meat department. Probe thermometer use and calibration were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Packages of foam trays were observed on the floor in the storage area of the meat department. Proper storage up off the floor was discussed. 
Single service and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 The following violations remain from the previous inspection.
1. Buildup of debris was observed under the dry storage shelving near the stairwell.
2. Wall and attached plumbing under the 3 part sink were soiled with splash.
3. Caulk was moldy and worn away at the wall juncture for the prep sink by the chicken breading station.
4. Floor drain cover under the deli 3 part sink was soiled with heavy buildup.
NOTE: Floor drains throughout have been cleaned since the previous inspection. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority items related to temperature abuse and date marking were observed during the inspection. Best practices for cooling were not observed, and foods in the process of cooling had to be reheated to begin the process again. A section of foods in the hot deli case were observed with internal temperatures below 135F, resulting reheating and/or discard of foods. Best practices were not observed for quick chilling and cold holding after preparation of foods intended for cold storage. Soups were discarded based on prep dates from February and/or lack of date marks. Also, two of the three handwashing sinks were without soup, and one of the handwashing sinks was soiled and slow draining. Educational handouts for date marking, cooling, and proper hot/cold holding temperatures were provided. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited during re-inspection on 3/21/22. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Deli manager has an expired food manager certification and is working to get certification along with all of the managers at this location. Once certifications are completed all managers and enough assistant managers should be certified to ensure the presence of a CFM during all hours of operation. In the meantime, the produce manager was on-site during the inspection and able to show proof of a current food manager certification.  
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Employee in dish area was observed chewing something and confirmed they had candy in their mouth when asked. Employee was advised to cease eating candy while working in the deli area. All foods, including candy and gum, should only be consumed in designated areas/at break time when employees are not working around food and/or clean dishes. Employee washed hands at request of inspector prior to continuing with ware washing. 
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Two of the three handwashing sinks were not properly stocked with hand soap. The handwashing sink across from the hot case had an empty soap dispenser, and the handwashing sink in the corner adjacent to chicken breading station had a soap dispenser with dead batteries. Soap from dispenser with dead batteries was moved to the other handwashing sink, and a pump bottle of hand soap was placed at the handwashing sink in the corner. Ensure batteries are changed as needed and all handwashing sinks are properly stocked.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Knives and a spreader were stored in the crevices between storage racks and the wall above the 3 part sink. The crevices between the racks and the wall are not considered clean surfaces and are not intended for storage of cleaned and sanitized utensils. Knives and spreader were removed to be re-washed and sanitized. Cease this storage practice.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Cooked foods prepared earlier today were in the walk-in cooler and observed with internal temperatures at 106F (sausage and peppers) and 108F-115F (three meatloaves). Cooling process began around 12-12:30pm based on information provided, and internal temperatures were observed during inspection at 2:50pm. Foods were placed back in the steamer to be reheated to 165F/above and restart the cooling process. Ensure temperatures are monitored during cooling process with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling. 
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Lasagna and gravy in the hot case had internal temperatures of 113F and 118F. Lasagna was placed in the steamer to reheat based on initial time of prep and gravy was discarded along with other foods the deli manager confirmed to have internal temperatures below 135F. The foods below 135F were all within the middle section of the holding case. Ensure the unit is able to maintain foods at proper temperature and consider placing the hot holding unit at a higher setting to offset for temperate loss during times when doors will be opened and closed frequently. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Several prepared foods intended to be cold held were observed on a cart in the prep area. Employee was working with and preparing multiple salads, sandwiches and other items. Surface temperatures ranged from 50F to 66F depending on how long items were out during prep within the last ~30-45 minutes. Employee was in the process of finishing prep and labeling containers. All foods were placed in the walk-in cooler to quickly chill foods. Best practice of only working with limited amounts of foods at a time was discussed. Foods should be rotated back into the the cooler to quickly chill once prep is done and prior to beginning preparation of other items.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 Containers of cooked and cooled soups in the chicken walk-in cooler had prep dates of 2/27 and 2/26. One container was without a date mark. Deli manager removed all products in question for discard. Ensure prepared foods are properly dated and used or discarded within 7 days, 
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Handwashing sink in the corner adjacent to the chicken breading station was slow draining. This handwashing sink was said to be the least frequently used and was observed to be soiled with general buildup, especially in the drain. Management was advised to clean the sink and have maintenance provide service to clear any potential debris and ensure proper drainage. 
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 1. General buildup was observed along the floor to wall juncture throughout the deli.
2. Buildup of debris was observed under the dry storage shelving near the stairwell.
3. Floor drains throughout the deli were soiled and in need of cleaning. 
4. Wall and attached plumbing under the 3 part sink were soiled with splash.
5. Caulk was moldy and worn away at the wall juncture for the prep sink by the chicken breading station. 
Cleaning and general maintenance of physical structures were discussed. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

No CFPM is observed at the facility during the inspection. A manager on the way out of th building at the beginning of the inspection stated that the managers all usually leave by 4:30 to 5:00 pm. PIC is instructed to ensure that a CFPM is on site at all times that the food handling operations are taking place.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

1) The hand sink on the side adjacent to the bakery area is observed without paper towel in the dispenser. 2) The hand sink next to the meat slicers is without paper towels on arrival. The meat slicers are observed in operation at this time. PIC was consulted and instructed to ensure that the hand sinks are properly supplied at all times. Paper towels were replaced during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination.

Multiple knives and spatulas are observed stored between the wall and holding racks above the three part sink. PIC instructed that this is not an easily cleanable location and that food contact items should not be stored here. Items removed to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
PRODUCE: Quat sanitizer observed to be dispensed from wall-mounted dispenser at ~100ppm. CORRECTED-- Staff can acquire sanitizer from other departments until dispenser is reaching appropriate sanitizing concentration. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have concentration based on label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
PRODUCE: No sanitizer bucket prepared at time of inspection. CORRECTED-- Sanitizer bucket prepared from wall-mounted dispenser in another department.
4-303.11: (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. [Pf]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

There was not a CFPM certification available for any employee at the time of the inspection. The difference between the food handler certification and the Certified Manager certification was discussed and the PIC is instructed to ensure that a CFPM is available in this area at all times food or food contact are handled.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani buckets in the prep areas are both observed lower than 100 ppm quat on the inspector's test strips. Quat based sanitizers should be at a minimum of 200 ppm. The buckets were remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. 

Multiple spatula and knives are observed stored above the 3 part sink with the food contact surfaces in the crack between the wall and the storage rack. This gap cannot be effectively cleaned/ sanitized and the utensils should be stored so that the food contact surfaces are not at risk of contamination.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
No CFM was present during inspection. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540. 

NOTE: Store director will attempt to provide documentation for CFM coverage for facility.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed employee (deli) place gloves on hands without properly washing hands between glove change. Ensure all employees wash hands before placing gloves on. Corrected. Education provided regarding glove use and handwashing. PIC will provide further information to employees. Reference 2-301.14.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Stand is not protected. No cover protects food against environment. (PIC will provide necessary protection). 

*TD 6/20/2019 1245: Overhead protection was at site. 
Reference 6-202.17.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed several handsinks with food equipment/utensils in sink. In addition, several handsinks had evidence of food and liquid disposal in sink. Ensure handsinks are accessible at all times. Ensure handsinks are for handwashing only. Corrected. Education Provided.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked by several lids of food equipment . Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: Observed several meats to be thawing at room temperature in front of meat department. Ensure proper thawing occurs for all frozen TCS food. Corrected. Education provided. Meat was moved to W-I cooler (Meat R.)
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Meat is thawing at room temperature. Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. Reference 3-501.13.
